notes: Chosen hook (index 0) 'ONE MOLECULE, 2 DRUG TARGETS'. Clarity: readable in under 2 seconds, big type, the yellow 2 gives a focal point. Curiosity: moderate; it raises 'how is that possible, and who did it?' The cover image (one strand bridging two spheres) reinforces the idea. Concrete number/name: only '2', and no company name on the cover (the tag says CHINA AI, not Tencent), so it is the weakest on name and specificity. Promise kept: yes. Slide 3 is titled 'One molecule, two targets' and the body explains dual-target peptides; slide 2 (the Nature paper) does not itself deliver the promise, but it is one swipe away. The cover does not overclaim and the animal-only caveat is on slide 6. Stake: none; the reader is not told what changes for them. Fine, because the articles state no effect on ordinary readers. Hook types: labels are honest (0 claim, 1 number, 2 claim, 3 number); none is reader-impact and none claims to be. hook_pick_reason starts with an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' reason (preclinical animal results only, human effect unverified). Other options: 3 ('TENCENT AI CUTS TUMOURS 94.2%') is the punchiest, with a name and a number, but it reads as a human or clinical result when it is animal-only and the cover cannot hold the qualifier, so it is a promise risk. 1 ('1/10 THE DOSE') has the same problem, is ambiguous out of context, and gives no subject beyond Tencent. 2 ('TENCENT'S FIRST NATURE PAPER') has a name but little curiosity for a global audience and is about the company, not the finding. Chosen is the best honest option. Optional improvement, not required: add Tencent to the tag, for example 'TENCENT AI · RESEARCH', for a name hook without a number risk.
